questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The specialisation "Forest and Nature Management in times of climate change" offered at the university of Göttingen resonated most with my interests and future career aspirations.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We received most of the relevant information per email and from the international student coordinator. It was also quite useful to talk to other students who had done the exchange before or studied at the university of Göttingen already for longer. There was always someone to ask for help.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my shared flat via the plattform WG-gesucht. I was quite lucky that I got the second flat I contacted, but I heard from others that they found it a bit harder to find accomodation on their own. I also recommend facebook groups if one would like to live in shared flats instead of student accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are two campi at the university of Göttingen, the Central Campus close to the city center and the North Campus. I lived directly at the Central Campus, but had most classes at the North Campus, so I basically lived "off North Campus". I really appreciated to be close to the city center and that I could use the larger libraries at the Central Campus. There are more students and more students stay in the library to study in the evenings, which I valued particularly in the exam period. However, one should be aware of the daily commuting times to the North Campus, which took about 15-20 minutes by bus or by bike one way.

questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Since I did not have a background in forestry, the level of courses was fine for me. However, for people with a background in forest and nature management, courses might have been perceived as repitition and a bit superficial.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was very different to the one at UCPH. First, there were less contact hours, i.e. only few hours of lectures each week and students were expected to study independently for the rest of the time. There was less group work, both in lectures and for assignments. Furthermore, the exams all took place at the end of the semester within 1-2 weeks, which increased the work load towards the semester much more. We also had only one oral exam, all the other exams were written. Generally, the atmosphere and relationship between students and teachers was much more anonymous than at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Master's thesis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Monitoring of Forest Resources: very useful knoweldge about design of data collection and statistics
Forest Management under Different Climatic Conditions: excursions and interesting insights into (German) forest management practices and climate change
Bioclimatology and Global Change: very essential basic knowledge about our climate system and Biosphere
Remote Sensing Image Processing with Open Source Software: very useful practical knowledge about the use of QGIS and Pyhthon

questions.answer: I recommend to participate in the university sports opportunities. There is a great offer and its an amazing way to meet other students also from other courses.

questions.answer: It was quite easy for me, but I was also quite familiar with the local culture of the exchange site.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I recommend to participate in the sports offers of the university or join other university groups.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Honesty and a very direct way to communicate

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The culture at the university can be quite anonymous and it could make the atmosphere seem a bit "cold". Don't be initmidated by this but be couragous to exchange with local people.
Dont stress yourself too much about the exams. Its a lot of content to study in a short time. Try to follow the lectures, take notes and ask questions during the semester. Towards the exams, I would recommend doing past papers! They are super helpful to get an idea about the set up of the exams. 
Please enjoy the city and your studies! I stressed far too much about the assignments and exams and missed to enjoy the rest a bit...

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *

questions.answer: The people I studied with!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To make choices from the great range of opportunities to engage in extracurriular activities and to manage time well between studies/exam preparation and hobbies.

questions.answer: Yes
